verdict.tagline: Stunning wilderness and deep tracking simulation hampered by technical friction.
for_you_if: you enjoy slow-paced and methodical tracking gameplay
you appreciate detailed and realistic natural environments
you have the patience for long hunts
not_for_you_if: you are bothered by extensive paid downloadable content
you need stable save files without corruption risks
you dislike losing tracking trails after long pursuits

single_points.text: One reviewer says that purchasing the Ultimate bundle does not give you everything and only includes a fraction of the available DLC.

citation.review_text:
BUYER BEWARE: Purchasing the "Ultimate" Bundle does not get you everything. Calling it that, implies that there is nothing more to purchase for a complete package. I don't care how good the game is; this is intentionally deceptive, and any company that does this is full of shit. Buying the "Ultimate" Hunting Bundle really only gets you roughly 30ish percent of the available DLC. 

From now on, I'm going to have to do extensive research before buying, to ensure that this doesn't happen again.

claims.claim: Reviewers report spending extended periods walking across large environments while tracking animals, leading to moments where finding targets feels difficult or tedious.

citations.review_text:
1/10 – One of the Most Frustrating Hunting Games I've Played

Honestly, this game is a massive disappointment. What could have been a fun and immersive hunting experience turns into hours of walking around, dealing with frustrating mechanics, and barely finding anything worth hunting.

The movement feels clunky, tracking animals can be tedious, and sometimes it feels like the animals have better AI than the actual game developers. The amount of patience this game demands is ridiculous, especially when you spend ages tracking something just for it to run off or disappear.

The bugs, awkward controls, and repetitive gameplay don't help either. Instead of feeling like an exciting hunting simulator, it often feels like a walking simulator with occasional shooting.

I understand the game is supposed to be realistic, but realistic doesn't have to mean boring, frustrating, and unnecessarily time-consuming.

Overall: A game with a lot of potential that gets ruined by tedious gameplay and frustrating mechanics. I wanted to go hunting, not spend half my life walking through a forest simulator.

this game is fun if you want to slowly run around the whole time till you can find a animal and miss the shot then spend more time running VERY SLOWLY to find the animal again then hit it the second time but the animal somehow runs faster than the speed of light and then is never seen again.

· You can't have a hot tomboy tradwife follow you around everywhere. Pretty self-explanatory. Trivially attainable in real life, but not in a power fantasy about bullying animals with 21st century technology? Please.

I would highly recommend theHunter: Call of the Wild because it is genuinely one of the greatest games ever created. The graphics are absolutely incredible, the environments are breathtaking, and the attention to detail is on a whole different level. Every map feels like a real place, with amazing wildlife, beautiful scenery, and endless opportunities to explore. The hunting experience is extremely realistic, making every animal encounter feel exciting and rewarding. Honestly, it is a masterpiece that deserves every bit of praise it gets, and I genuinely believe everyone should experience this legendary game at least once in their lifetime.

Hunter: Call of the Wild — A Love Letter to What Was Lost

Two hundred hours.

Two hundred hours beneath golden sunsets, through forests that whispered secrets, across valleys where the fog clung to the earth like a dying dream. Two hundred hours of patience, of footsteps softened by grass, of holding my breath as antlers emerged between the trees. Two hundred hours spent chasing the wild, and somehow, the wild became a part of me.

And now, it is gone.

My trophies, my rifles, my hard-earned fortunes. The animals I tracked across continents, the lodges that once held the memories of countless hunts. All vanished into the indifferent silence of an empty save file. The wilderness remembers nothing, it seems. It does not mourn the hunter who once walked its trails.

Yet, I cannot bring myself to hate this game.

For what is the Hunter: Call of the Wild if not a reminder that beauty was never meant to be possessed? The forests still stand. The rivers still run. The deer still wander through the morning mist, unaware that their greatest adversary has been reduced to a beginner's rifle and an empty inventory.

And so, I return.

Not as the hunter I was, adorned with trophies and experience, but as a stranger to my own wilderness. Once more, I will stumble through the undergrowth. Once more, I will mistake a distant call for something closer. Once more, I will spend forty minutes tracking an animal, only to discover that I have been following my own footsteps in a circle.
And I will love every miserable second of it.

Because the progress was never truly the point. It was the quiet mornings, the distant thunder, the sudden heartbeat when a magnificent creature stepped into view. It was the feeling of being impossibly small in a world that did not care whether I succeeded.

Two hundred hours have disappeared, but the memories remain.

claims.claim: Reviewers experience technical bugs where animal sounds like fleeing or mating calls cannot be heard, and animals occasionally freeze or run in place during longer sessions.

citations.review_text:
Pretty awesome game. Been playing on and off since 2021. Have a couple things I don't love still, for example when riding around on the four wheeler when you get off sometimes it randomly decides you can't pull anything out of your inventory. Thankfully if you open and close the camera it fixes itself, in that moment. I have also noticed that if you have a longer session (this is when it happens to me not sure what triggers this) animals get weird. I've been able to walk up to things and they are running in place or just frozen. Sometimes they unfreeze and freak out.

Overall though, I love this game. Its not super easy (it is kind of  a pay to win game but all the dlc is cheap especially when on sale) but once you find enough zones it becomes a lot easier to grind for cash.
It has many hours of fun from classic small game to fighting for your life surrounded by a pack of wolves.
They took way better care of this game this than they did with their fishing game, this game is 100x better. Very worth giving it a try.


After 210 hours and I am still figuring out tricks to be better.

This game is great, but it has too many bugs.  Every time they release new DLC, they introduce new bugs.  For instance, this year they released new DLC, but the dog DLC didn't work any more for a couple of months.  It took them years to fix trophies missing in your lodges.  Now, for the last several months, you can't hear fleeing or mating animal calls at times (mammal or birds), and this has been a long term issue.  It's called call of the wild...  You can't hear the call! If you want to play, you're are going to experience bugs with more on the way.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the maps as beautiful and unique with an impressive roster of diverse animals and trophies.

citations.review_text:
Whether you enjoy casual hunting where you walk a map and shoot whatever you see, or you like to grind out the best of the best, this game has you covered. The maps are beautiful, each one unique, and the animal roster is impressive. You get 2 new maps per year and several new animals as well, keeping the content fun and engaging. 

The only criticism I have is that it does seem like some community complaints fall on deaf ears when it comes to bug fixes or recommendations wanted by the community as a whole. I personally have not experienced this disappointment, but I have seen enough from the community to know that it seems to be a problem. 

I thoroughly enjoy this game and find myself always coming back to complete missions or search for diamonds and hope one day I might spawn a great one.

A fun challenge. The maps are beautiful, the models are great, and the gameplay loop is enjoyable. There's something immensely satisfying in completing a stalk on an animal and getting a dream trophy to add to your lodge. The customization is satisfactory, and there's not much I can complain about. A solid hunting game overall.

Excellent jeu avec 500+ heures de jeu, je le recommande énormément ! Le plus fun, c’est de chercher à obtenir les plus gros trophées, classés en bronze, argent, or et diamant. Sans parler de leur esthétique ! Un diamant, par exemple, aura un score très élevé et, chez les cervidés, un ÉNORME panache, sans exagération !
Visuellement, le jeu est très beau aussi ! En tout cas, personnellement, je m’amuse énormément depuis sa sortie, et le jeu reste quand même bien entretenu, avec de nouveaux DLC régulièrement.

----------------------------------

Excellent game with 500+ hours of gameplay. I highly recommend it! The most fun part is hunting for the biggest trophies, ranked as Bronze, Silver, Gold, and Diamond. Not to mention their appearance! A Diamond trophy, for example, will have a very high score, and when it comes to deer, they have HUGE antlers! No exaggeration!
The game is also visually stunning! Personally, I’ve had a blast playing it since its release, and the game is still being well maintained, with new DLCs being released regularly.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that essential features, weapons, and quality-of-life additions are locked behind paid downloadable content packs.

citations.review_text:
I used to enjoy relaxing with this game, but I can no longer support it. It has completely transformed into a lazy, overpriced cash grab.
The developers consistently ignore the community. Rather than fixing the robotic animal AI or updating broken mechanics, they just pump out paid DLC and unrealistic "Great One" grinds. Vital gameplay items are locked behind a paywall, making the full game cost over $300. The publisher has a history of abandoning games once profit slows down. Save your money. 
#StopKillingGames

As others have said - This game needs a major ai overhaul, old models need to be brought to date, prices need to be lowered/tiny dlc need to be bundled to stop buying pack for 1 item in em for 5 dollars per (tent, tripod, goose decoy, mallard decoy, electronic caller, ect), necessary qol dlc needs to be unlisted and added to this already expensive game, and we need a big quality of life mass overhaul. 

For example - traveling for hours on foot to the reserves just to unlock the map so you can do what you came to do, hunt, the point of the game- nty. 

Inventory management and weight is also busted, in a bad way. 

My final additional opinion: We should have like 5 basemaps, keep our reserve dlc, but take the small dlcs and make em a higher value low price dlc, or just add em to the game, because the dlc amount for the priced they are is absolutely wild, and unsustainable for people in this day and age. 

This game, my main point, is also REALLY good at creating a problem to sell you a solution. Unbearable travel? Spend 5 dollars usd (way more if you have a low conversion rate), to make travel faster but still painful on a supposedly off road vehicle while scaring away everything within a literal half mile radius. 

Kills really hard to find and tedious to collect, resulting in losing them? Buy a dog! 

How about very, very minimal base game weapons that can barely get you through a full roster on a base game map? Here's 5 dlc to buy because there's only 1 relevant weapon in each pack. 

Yes, negative review, but I LOVE this game. I've spent a lot of time, and a good chunk of money on it, and I'm still having fun and want to play it for as long as I can, as often as I can. But people should earn their money, and they should respect their customer base, which this company is slacking on, pretty hard. 

Would I reccomend this game? Maybe. But only if you're an adult with money to spend, time to sink, and a whole lot of patience to research non-intuitive mechanics.

Lo…

I really did enjoy this game. I owned it on both console and PC for many years. Over that time, I've seen countless paid DLCs drop. I've purchased a few maps and lodges, but it's getting frustrating. Every other developer provides FREE updates for their players. Most of the weapons packs, blinds, and bird hunting features should have been free. Or instead, give regular players a few new maps. It's exhausting seeing every new feature come with a price tag. I refuse to pay any more. Please do better.
